subject: Private Offer: tiered SKU + channel margin uplift proposal
messages:
From: Alex Brown <alex.brown@amazon.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: CloudScale RevOps <revops@cloudscale.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: AWS Private Offer — initial tiered SKU and channel margin ask

Vanessa,

Great speaking yesterday. AWS has sketched a private-offer frame for CloudScale (prospect) that accelerates procurement — they want a 3-tier seat-based SKU (developer / team / enterprise) with graduated list prices and an explicit reseller commission schedule.

High level asks from AWS/CloudScale:
- Can Redwood support a private offer with per-seat SKUs that allow list price differentiation by tier?
- CloudScale expects a 12–20% effective channel margin depending on committed ARR; can Redwood offer a margin waterfall or co-funding model to hit that range?
- Can we co-fund a 3-month POC credit (up to $25k) on the private-offer invoice to help close the deal?

I've attached the term sheet outline and a suggested mapping of SKUs to tier names (attached: private_offer_term_sheet.pdf, sku_mapping.csv). AWS would prefer a signed commitment by 3/29 to meet their marketplace calendar.

Alex
Alex Brown | AWS Partner Development
alex.brown@amazon.com

Subject: Re: AWS Private Offer — initial tiered SKU and channel margin ask

Alex — thanks for the clear summary and attachments. Looping in Karthik (Marketplace/Finance) and Priyom (Channel Ops) to confirm commercial constraints. A few quick clarifying Qs for CloudScale:

1) The 12–20% stated — is that target effective margin after AWS fees, or target gross margin before AWS marketplace fees?
2) Is the POC credit refundable/recoupable if we land the deal, or a pure defender to accelerate the PO?
3) Do they need list-price parity across regions or can we scope this strictly to us-east-1 (single-region private offer)?

From Redwood's side, we support tiered SKUs on marketplace private offers. We need to validate:
- list-price mapping to SKU IDs (we'll use sku_mapping.csv as a baseline)
- whether they want Redwood to show a partner commission line item (some resellers prefer visible commissions)
- the trial credit handling — whether it posts as a discount on the private offer invoice or as a separate credit we process off-platform.

Karthik/Priyom — can you weigh in on feasible margin waterfalls and whether we can cost-share a $25k POC under our current committed discount windows?

Thanks,
Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz | Sr. Channel Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 14:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AWS Private Offer — initial tiered SKU and channel margin ask

Vanessa — quick calc from finance lens. Some assumptions up front: AWS marketplace takes ~6% handling + transaction fees; list price waterfall is the lever we can use, plus a short-term co-funding credit that Redwood can approve for strategic deals.

Proposal (high level):
- Developer SKU: list $0.10 / seat / hour (low price point) — target partner margin 12% post-AWS fees
- Team SKU: list $0.22 / seat / hour — target partner margin 15% post-AWS fees
- Enterprise SKU: list $0.45 / seat / hour — target partner margin 20% post-AWS fees with a 12-month commit

Co-funding: we can approve up to $20k in POC credits for marketplace private offers if deal meets:
- minimum ARR commit of $150k ARR when annualized post-POC, and
- signed reseller agreement with 60-day SLA to convert the POC to paid seat count.

Visibility: finance prefers partner commission visible as a separate line on the invoice for bookkeeping. If CloudScale insists on a higher band, we can run a one-off uplift with Product + Finance signoff; lead time ~3 business days.

If CloudScale can confirm the ARR commitment threshold and whether the POC credit is considered a recoverable contra-revenue item, we can fast-track approval.

-Karthik
Head, Marketplace Finance | Redwood Inference

From: CloudScale RevOps <revops@cloudscale.com>
To: Alex Brown <alex.brown@amazon.com>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AWS Private Offer — initial tiered SKU and channel margin ask

Vanessa / Alex / Karthik — thanks. A few specifics from CloudScale's commercial team:

- The 12–20% target is net to us after AWS fees (i.e., what our sales team keeps). We need a visible commission line and clarity on recurring vs. one-time commission for seat add-ons during year 1.
- We'll commit to a 12-month initial term for Enterprise tier if Redwood will support the 20% band at scale (we can agree to a 12-month ramp: 14% first 3 months, 17% next 3, 20% after month 6 contingent on ARR targets).
- POC credit: we'd prefer it to be co-funded and applied as a discount on the private-offer invoice so it flows through the marketplace. If Redwood cannot do that, we'll accept an off-invoice credit but will need a reconciliation statement for bookkeeping.
- ARR threshold: we can commit to $200k ARR annualized post-POC for Enterprise to unlock the top-tier margin.

Please confirm the waterfall mechanics and whether Redwood can sign a simple amendment that makes the POC credit recoverable if the customer churns within 90 days.

Thanks,
S. Patel
Head, RevOps | CloudScale
revops@cloudscale.com
From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: CloudScale RevOps <revops@cloudscale.com>, Alex Brown <alex.brown@amazon.com>

Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AWS Private Offer — initial tiered SKU and channel margin ask

S, Alex — appreciate the clear commitments. Summary / agreed next steps from Redwood: 

1) We support tiered SKUs on a private offer scoped to us-east-1 for this transaction.
2) Redwood can make partner commission visible on-invoice. We'll model the waterfall as: 14% (months 1–3) / 17% (months 4–6) / 20% (month 7+) conditional on hitting the $200k ARR threshold.
3) Redwood can co-fund up to $20k of POC credit applied as a marketplace discount on the private-offer invoice; credit will be structured as recoverable contra-revenue if the customer cancels within 90 days. Finance will include the reconciliation appendix in the term sheet.
4) To proceed we need CloudScale signature on the reseller addendum and an executed PO by 3/29.

I'll circulate an updated term sheet (with the waterfall table and recoverability clause) by EOD tomorrow. If that looks good we'll ask AWS to create the private-offer draft.

Thanks — excited to move this forward.
Vanessa
Sr. Channel Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
